podcast.body: Featured on the "Smash" album, this song contains the notable lyric "keep them separated." "Come out and play, keep them separated."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: The first single from *Smash*, "Come Out and Play" gained massive traction after being played on an LA radio station, leading to a quick $5,000 music video funded by Epitaph Records. The song famously features Jason McClain, the band's number one fan and a forklift operator, contributing the line "you gotta keep them separated." "Come out and play the first single from the offspring's 1994 album, Smash. And one of their songs, one of the offspring songs, had somehow made it onto an LA radio station and was getting a massive response. Then MTV called, where's the video? So Epitaph sunk $5,000 into making a quickie clip."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This single from The Offspring's 1994 album "Smash" is associated with the record-breaking sales of the album, which holds the title of the biggest selling indie rock record of all time. "The offspring with Kamada and Play, a single from the biggest selling indie rock record of all time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Book of World Records Version 1.0 - Part 1

podcast.body: This song became a hit, first receiving mainstream radio airplay in Los Angeles, which then led to the entire "Smash" album becoming massively popular. "When come on and play became a hit, the whole album blew up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
